evidence.title: RBNZ hold surprise and subsequent hawkish offset
evidence.facts: The complete official October 28 record confirms a 4-3 hold at 2.75%, against widely expected October tightening. The majority cited lower-than -expected inflation, smaller indirect fuel-price effects, subdued wages, weak consumption/investment and time to observe two previous hikes. Core near the upper target band and broader price increases were largely expected, rather than evidence of a fresh upside surprise. All members still see tighter policy likely, conditional on the outlook; the record explicitly allows future holds or easing if global demand deteriorates sharply. RNZ reports Westpac economist Eckhold observed the one-year swap rate down about 20 bp after the decision on October 28. That report is an attributed event-time observation, not a new/current October 29 yield measurement. Later conference remarks about further hikes and imported inflation are substantial opposition to weakness. The October 29 Herald interview is now verified separately; this does not verify every scheduled broadcast. Wholesale-to-retail rate pass-through and cost-to-CPI pass-through are distinct; no mechanical rate conclusion is drawn from either.
evidence.timing_note: Original source date retained. Publication/update hour not independently established; verification does not redate the release.

evidence.title: NZ ANZ survey: resilient demand and firmer price-setting intentions
evidence.facts: Original ANZ October report: business confidence 52.5 versus 51.9; own-activity outlook 46.2 versus 47.9; past activity 15.0 versus 10.8. Pricing intentions 52.2 versus 48.4; intended three-month price increase 1.92% versus 1.76%; one-year inflation expectations 3.31% versus 3.25%. Cost expectations remained 81.9; expected wage growth eased to 2.79% from 2.83%. Investment intentions eased to 18.3 from 22.6 and employment intentions to 17.4 from 17.9. ANZ describes resilient demand and only marginal wage upside risk to RBNZ forecasts. The headline confidence improvement alone understates both firmer price-setting and softer forward investment/own activity. These components form one release package. Pepperstone event 554040002/value 280445 still had no actual, forecast 48.1 and capture October 22; the direct ANZ release takes priority without overwriting the raw broker observation. There is no independently verified unique survey consensus.
evidence.timing_note: ANZ PDF dated October 29; exact PDF publication hour unknown. 00:00 UTC is the broker scheduled release, not independently verified actual publication. Reuters survey report displays 00:11 UTC, and the full source was verified later this review.
